guideTitle: Best Air Fryers With Dial Controls (2026)
metaTitle: Best Air Fryers With Dial Controls in 2026
metaDescription: Six air fryers with real knobs and dials compared across basket and toaster-oven styles, with timer lengths, temperature ranges and cleanup notes.
expertTake: The Cuisinart 1800W air fryer toaster oven is the best dial-controlled pick because a mechanical temperature dial, a 60 minute timer and 0.6 cubic feet of room make it a full oven replacement. The Uten 5.8 qt with a 60 minute timer is the best dial basket. Skip dials if you want presets or app control, since this class offers neither.
introParagraphs: Most new air fryers have moved to touch screens, which makes a dial-controlled unit a deliberate choice. Knobs are quick to set, readable without glasses and hard to break, and they keep working long after a touch panel might have failed.

The trade-off is that dial machines usually skip presets and smart features. What you get instead is direct control, a short learning curve and a build that is easy to understand, which suits plenty of cooks better than a menu.

products.name: Cuisinart 1800W air fryer toaster oven, 8-in-1
products.description:
Cuisinart's toaster oven combines eight functions, including air fry, convection, broil and warm, with an adjustable temperature dial and a sixty minute timer that doubles as an auto shut-off. The 0.6 cubic foot interior is described as large enough for six slices of toast or three pounds of fries.

A mechanical dial and a long timer make this the easiest model here to operate by feel. Compared with the basket-style Uten and Dash units, it is a different type of machine, with racks and a door instead of a drawer. That gives you a toaster oven's range and an air fryer's crisp in one body.

The interior wipes down and the crumb tray slides out for cleaning. Plan for a wide footprint and several inches of clearance on every side. A toast shade control adds the familiar toaster feel. Because the dial is mechanical, temperatures are approximate, so an inexpensive oven thermometer on the rack tells you how far the setting drifts. Rotate the tray halfway through for even colour, since the fan at the top pushes air harder across the back. Owners who bake as well as air fry usually value the long timer more than any single preset.
products.bestFor: Cooks who want a dial-controlled toaster oven that also air fries.
pros: Temperature dial and sixty minute timer
Auto shut-off at the end of the timer
0.6 cu ft interior fits six slices of toast
Eight functions including broil and warm
cons: Wide body takes real counter space
Rack cooking needs tray turning for even browning

products.name: Cuisinart 1800W air fryer oven with grill, 8-in-1

specList.label: Functions
specList.value: Bake, convection bake, grill, broil, warm

products.description:
This Cuisinart variant keeps the same 1800 watt dial-controlled oven but adds a grill function alongside bake, convection bake, broil and warm. The listing echoes the same large interior and the same adjustable temperature dial.

The grill function is the difference. It suits steaks, chops and vegetables that want char, and it gives the oven a second personality beyond air frying. Against the other Cuisinart, the choice comes down to whether you will use the grill, since the control scheme is identical.

The cleanup routine is the same, with a removable crumb tray and a wipe-down interior. Grilling does produce more splatter, so wipe the walls after fatty cooks. Keep clear space around the oven during use. Preheat the grill setting for a few minutes before searing, since a cold element gives grey rather than charred results. Pat meat dry first, and expect some smoke from fatty cuts in a small kitchen, so run the extractor fan. If grilling is rare for you, the plain version covers nearly everything else the same way.
products.bestFor: Cooks who want a grill setting on a dial-controlled oven.

products.name: Uten 5.8 qt air fryer, 1700W, 60-minute dials
products.description:
Uten offers a 5.8 quart basket with mechanical temperature and timer dials, a sixty minute timer and a 1700 watt element. The temperature runs from about 160F to 400F, and the unit auto-pauses if the basket is pulled out.

The listing mentions a stainless steel material and says the basket can handle a whole chicken of five to six pounds. For a dial-controlled basket, that is a rare combination of capacity and long timer. Compared with the Dash, it is larger, and compared with the Cuisinart, it is a basket rather than an oven.

The auto-pause feature is the sort of safeguard that older machines lack. Do the basket by hand and wipe the housing weekly. Give the vents room and use a wall outlet. A long timer is a mixed blessing: it enables roasts and cakes, but it also lets a forgotten basket run for an hour, so stay in earshot. The auto-pause is a quiet safety win in a house with children. Compared with the thirty minute sibling, this is the one to buy if you ever roast a whole bird or bake in the basket.
products.bestFor: Cooks who want a roomy basket with mechanical dials.
pros: 5.8 qt basket handles a whole chicken
Sixty minute timer for long cooks
Auto-pause when the basket is removed
Mechanical dials with little to fail

products.name: Uten 5.8 qt air fryer, 1700W, timer knob
products.description:
This earlier Uten version uses a temperature knob from 175F to 400F and a timer knob that runs up to thirty minutes. The listing also says it can cook a normal-sized chicken, which sets it apart from smaller baskets.

Thirty minutes covers almost every air fryer job, and the knob feels familiar to anyone who has used an old kitchen timer. Next to the sixty minute Uten, it gives up the longer cycle and auto-pause in exchange for a simpler spec. Against the Dash, it is far larger.

The 5.8 quart basket is wider than a compact unit, so it needs space on the counter. Rinse the basket by hand and clean the housing. A silicone mat helps keep it from walking across a smooth surface. The knob sets time by sweeping a spring, so turn it forward past ten minutes and back to the number you want, which is how most mechanical timers behave. Expect a loud tick while it counts down. For most households the thirty minute limit never gets in the way.
products.bestFor: Cooks who want a large basket and simple knobs.
pros: Familiar timer knob up to thirty minutes
cons: Timer tops out at thirty minutes

products.name: Dash Tasti-Crisp 2.6 qt air fryer with dials
products.description:
Dash offers two dials, one for temperature up to 400F and one for a thirty minute timer. The 2.6 quart basket suits one or two people, and the listing describes it as compact enough to fit on most counters.

Turn-and-go cooking is the whole appeal. There are no menus and no screens, and cooking is a matter of setting the two dials and waiting for the bell. Compared with the Uten units, it is much smaller, and compared with the Cuisinart ovens, it is far lighter.

Cleanup is simple, with a basket and pan that lift out. Because the unit is light, a non-slip mat helps. Space behind it lets the vent work. Beginners often overfill a small basket, so cook half a load first and note the time that works. Write that time on a sticky label near the machine. Over a few weeks you will build your own preset list, which is the quiet charm of dials.
products.bestFor: One or two people who want the simplest possible controls.
pros: Light basket is easy to lift
cons: No keep warm or preset modes

products.name: Dash Tasti-Crisp AirCrisp compact air fryer
products.description:
This Dash model uses AirCrisp technology in a compact design with adjustable temperature control and a timer dial. The listing highlights an auto shut-off feature and includes a recipe guide.

The recipe guide is a real help for a first-time owner who has no idea what temperature to use for a given food. Compared with the 2.6 quart Dash, this one focuses on safety and guidance. Against the Uten units, it is much smaller and simpler.

Wash the nonstick basket by hand and wipe the housing weekly. Keep the unit on a stable surface with space behind for the vent. Using the guide as a starting point saves wasted batches. Treat its times as a baseline and trim a minute if your food browns early. Because the unit is small, it suits households that cook one portion at a time and want a shut-off to catch lapses of attention.
products.bestFor: First-time owners who want dials, auto shut-off and a recipe guide.
cons: Small basket suits one or two people

buyingCriteria.explanation: Dial-controlled air fryers come in two shapes: baskets and toaster ovens. The Uten and Dash units are baskets, and the Cuisinart models are ovens with racks and a door. Baskets crisp food fastest in small batches. Ovens handle toast, pizza and sheet-pan meals. Decide which job you need first. If you already own a toaster oven you are happy with, a basket adds speed without duplicating it. If your toaster oven is failing, the Cuisinart replaces it and air fries as a bonus, which is the better use of one counter slot.

The Cuisinart and the Uten 60 minute unit offer an hour on the dial, while the Dash and the older Uten stop at thirty minutes. Most air frying finishes within thirty, but roasts and bakes can need longer. A sixty minute timer also acts as an auto shut-off on the oven. A mechanical timer that rings but does not cut power is a different thing, so read the listing for which behaviour you get. Never rely on a bell alone for a long roast.

The Uten lists roughly 160F to 400F for the 60 minute unit and 175F to 400F for the knob version. The Dash tops out at 400F. A low floor helps with reheating and warming, and a 400F ceiling covers most frozen foods.

Mechanical controls are simple, but safety still matters. The Uten 60 minute model auto-pauses when the basket is pulled out, and the Cuisinart ovens shut off at the end of the timer. The Dash AirCrisp lists auto shut-off. Check the listing for what each model actually does.
Baskets are quicker to clean than ovens. The Cuisinart has a crumb tray and wipe-down walls, while the Uten and Dash have one basket each. A grill function adds splatter, so expect more wiping.
The Cuisinart is the largest, followed by the Uten at 5.8 quarts, then the Dash. Measure your space and plan for clearance behind. A machine you cannot place comfortably will not get used.

howWeEvaluated.title: Genuine dial control
howWeEvaluated.description: We kept only models whose listing describes dials or knobs for temperature and time. We left out touch-screen units that merely have one dial. All six picks use mechanical controls.

howWeEvaluated.title: Timer and range
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared timer lengths and temperature ranges. The Cuisinart and Uten 60 minute units offer an hour, and the Dash stops at thirty. A longer timer suits roasts.

howWeEvaluated.title: Safety and auto features
howWeEvaluated.description: We read for auto shut-off, auto-pause and similar safeguards. The Uten and Cuisinart models list them. Simple controls do not replace safety features.

howWeEvaluated.title: Ownership and cleanup
howWeEvaluated.description: We tallied removable parts and checked the coating notes. Baskets wash quickly, and ovens need wall wiping. Dials generally outlast touch panels.

howWeEvaluated.title: Size and value
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared footprint and capacity against each tier. The Cuisinart is largest and the Dash is smallest. Prices differ between sellers, so we rated each machine by tier, not by figure.

cards.label: Basket
cards.text: The Uten and Dash baskets crisp food quickly in small batches. They are simpler and cheaper, and they need less counter space.

cards.label: Oven
cards.text: The Cuisinart models handle toast, pizza and sheet-pan meals as well as air frying. They are larger and need more clearance.

howToChoose.note: Choose a basket for speed and an oven for range.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: Look for large, clear knobs, a timer that suits your cooking and a safety feature. Avoid models that hide key settings behind a screen.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The Cuisinart oven is the best all-round dial machine. The Uten 60 minute basket is the best dial basket, and the Dash is the simplest.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You want a toaster oven replacement, which points to the Cuisinart. A longer timer and auto-pause also justify the Uten 60 minute model.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You cook small portions. The Dash covers that at the lowest tier.

maintenance.why: Fat sets on a nonstick surface within a day. A soft sponge preserves the finish.
Crumbs scorch and smoke on the next heat. Slide the tray out and tip it into a bin.
Grill splatter bakes onto the walls. A damp cloth with the oven cool removes it.
A loose dial can mislead you about the setting. Stop using the unit if it slips.
A warm plug on an 1800 watt load is a hazard. Replace or retire the unit if it discolours.

faq.q: Why choose an air fryer with dials?
faq.a: Dials are quick to set, easy to read and unlikely to fail. They suit cooks who dislike menus or touch screens. The trade-off is fewer presets and smart features.
Mechanical dials give approximate settings, so use them as a guide and check food early. For most air frying that precision is enough. Baking and delicate foods benefit from an oven thermometer.

faq.q: What is the difference between basket and oven styles?
faq.a: A basket cooks in a small drawer and crisps quickly. An oven has racks and a door, and it also toasts and bakes. The oven takes much more counter space.
For most air frying, yes. Roasts and cakes can need longer, which is where the sixty minute Cuisinart and Uten models help.

Often, since there is less electronics to fail. The nonstick coating is still a wear item. Gentle hand washing extends its life. A knob that develops play or a timer that stops ringing is the usual first fault, and both are visible long before the machine fails outright.

faq.q: Can I run these on any outlet?
faq.a: Use a wall outlet and avoid extension cords. The Cuisinart lists 1800W and the Uten lists 1700W, which is close to a standard circuit limit.
